249	    /* Drain any prior signal so we wait for *this* write's completion. */

256	        LOG_WARN("FBL: CDC_Write rejected, r=%d\r\n", (int)r);
257	        return false;

261	    if (xSemaphoreTake(s_write_done, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS)) != pdTRUE)
262	    {
263	        LOG_WARN("FBL: write timeout, marking detached\r\n");

267	    if (s_last_write_result != USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
268	    {
269	        LOG_WARN("FBL: write completion err=%d\r\n", (int)s_last_write_result);
270	        return false;
271	    }
272	    s_last_sent_byte = tx_byte;
273	    return true;
274	}

276	static void fretboard_link_task(void *param)
277	{
278	    (void)param;
279	
280	    LOG_INFO("FBL: fretboard link started\r\n");
281	
282	    uint8_t last_mask = 0u;
283	
284	    for (;;)
285	    {
286	        if (s_cdc_obj_valid && s_cdc_handle == USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE_INVALID)
287	        {
288	            s_cdc_obj_valid = false;

293	        if (xQueueReceive(s_cmd_queue, &mask, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS)) == pdTRUE)

295	            last_mask = mask;
296	        }
297	        else
298	        {
299	            mask = last_mask;
300	        }
301	
302	        if (s_connected)
303	        {
304	            (void)send_one_byte(mask);
305	        }
306	    }
307	}
308	
309	/* Pull bytes off the RX stream buffer and emit one PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW
310	 * per parsed 12-byte frame. Resync logic mirrors tools/ds_monitor.py: a
311	 * frame is valid only when buf[0]==0x03 AND buf[11]==0xFC; otherwise drop
312	 * the leading byte and retry alignment. The FSM-free buffered approach is
313	 * easier to reason about than a state machine and the frame is short. */
314	static void fretboard_rx_task(void *param)
315	{
316	    (void)param;
317	
318	    uint8_t  frame[DS_FRAME_LEN];
319	    size_t   filled = 0u;
320	    uint32_t parsed = 0u;
321	    uint32_t skipped_bytes = 0u;
322	
323	    for (;;)
324	    {
325	        size_t want = DS_FRAME_LEN - filled;
326	        size_t got  = xStreamBufferReceive(s_rx_stream, &frame[filled],
327	                                           want, portMAX_DELAY);
328	        if (got == 0u) { continue; }
329	        filled += got;
330	        if (filled < DS_FRAME_LEN) { continue; }
331	
332	        if (frame[0] != DS_START_BYTE || frame[DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u] != DS_END_BYTE)
333	        {
334	            /* Misaligned: drop one byte and shift, then loop to refill. */
335	            memmove(&frame[0], &frame[1], DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u);
336	            filled = DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u;
337	            skipped_bytes++;
338	            continue;
339	        }
340	
341	        uint16_t adc[FRET_COUNT];
342	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
343	        {
344	            adc[i] = (uint16_t)frame[1u + i * 2u]
345	                   | (uint16_t)((uint16_t)frame[2u + i * 2u] << 8);
346	        }
347	
348	        /* seq: u32 LE at bytes 11-14, applied_mask: u8 at byte 15. */
349	        uint32_t fb_seq = (uint32_t)frame[11]
350	                        | ((uint32_t)frame[12] << 8)
351	                        | ((uint32_t)frame[13] << 16)
352	                        | ((uint32_t)frame[14] << 24);
353	        uint8_t  applied_mask = frame[15];
354	
355	        Video_FrameInfo info;
356	        Video_GetFrameInfo(&info);
357	        PerfLog_EmitFretboardRaw(adc, info.frame_count, fb_seq, applied_mask);
358	
359	        parsed++;
360	        if (parsed == 1u || (parsed % 240u) == 0u)
361	        {
362	            LOG_DEBUG("FBL: rx parsed=%u skipped=%u G=%u R=%u Y=%u B=%u O=%u\r\n",
363	                      (unsigned)parsed, (unsigned)skipped_bytes,
364	                      (unsigned)adc[0], (unsigned)adc[1], (unsigned)adc[2],
365	                      (unsigned)adc[3], (unsigned)adc[4]);
366	        }
367	
368	        filled = 0u;
369	    }
370	}

372	void FretboardLink_Initialize(void)
373	{
374	    s_cmd_queue = xQueueCreateStatic(FBL_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH,
375	                                     sizeof(uint8_t),
376	                                     s_cmd_queue_storage,
377	                                     &s_cmd_queue_buf);
378	    configASSERT(s_cmd_queue != NULL);
379	
380	    s_write_done = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_write_done_buf);
381	    configASSERT(s_write_done != NULL);
382	
383	    s_ctrl_done = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_ctrl_done_buf);
384	    configASSERT(s_ctrl_done != NULL);
385	
386	    /* Storage array is FBL_RX_STREAM_BYTES + 1 per FreeRTOS — the +1 byte is
387	     * used by the buffer impl, not application data. Pass the *application*
388	     * size, not the storage size, as xBufferSizeBytes. */
389	    s_rx_stream = xStreamBufferCreateStatic(FBL_RX_STREAM_BYTES, 1u,
390	                                            s_rx_stream_storage,
391	                                            &s_rx_stream_buf);
392	    configASSERT(s_rx_stream != NULL);
393	
394	    /* Register the CDC attach listener before the bus is enabled — the host
395	     * stack only matches a class driver if its attach handler is in place
396	     * when enumeration completes. App-level USB_HOST_BusEnable runs right
397	     * after this init returns. */
398	    (void)USB_HOST_CDC_AttachEventHandlerSet(cdc_attach_handler, 0u);
399	
400	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_link_task,
401	                                       "FretLink",
402	                                       FBL_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
403	                                       NULL,
404	                                       FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
405	                                       s_task_stack,
406	                                       &s_task_tcb);
407	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK, h);
408	
409	    TaskHandle_t hr = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_rx_task,
410	                                        "FretRx",
411	                                        FBL_RX_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
412	                                        NULL,
413	                                        FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
414	                                        s_rx_task_stack,
415	                                        &s_rx_task_tcb);
416	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_RX, hr);
417	}
418	
419	bool FretboardLink_IsConnected(void)
420	{
421	    return s_connected;
422	}
423	
424	void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask, uint8_t producer_id)
425	{
426	    if (s_cmd_queue == NULL) { return; }
427	    uint8_t v = (uint8_t)(mask & TIMING_BIT_VALID_MASK);
428	    /* Overwrite is strictly latest-wins: a newer producer's mask replaces
429	     * any unsent older one — keeps a stalled USB write from accumulating
430	     * stale chord state. */
431	    (void)xQueueOverwrite(s_cmd_queue, &v);
432	
433	    uint8_t strum_dir = 0u;
434	    if      (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN) { strum_dir = 1u; }
435	    else if (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP)   { strum_dir = 2u; }
436	
437	    PerfLog_EmitActuator(v, s_last_sent_byte, strum_dir, producer_id,
438	                         s_last_ack_result, s_last_ack_ts_counter);
439	}

9	/* Fretboard link — USB CDC host writer that ferries a 7-bit GPIO bitmask
10	 * to the fretboard MCU as a stream of single-byte messages. Spec §4.4
11	 * actuator transport. Initialize first among the actuator modules so the
12	 * submit queue exists by the time any producer task starts running. Also
13	 * enables the USB host bus, so call after SYS_Initialize.
14	 *
15	 * Producers — timing_pipeline today, manual_control during operator UI
16	 * mode, future game menu controller (spec §4.8) — all submit through
17	 * FretboardLink_Send and tag themselves with a perf_actuator_producer_t
18	 * id. The id rides on the PERF_REC_ACTUATOR record emitted per Send so
19	 * the host can see which producer owns the wire at any moment (mode-level
20	 * arbitration is invisible from the wire byte alone).
21	 *
22	 * Latest-wins semantics: a newer mask overwrites an unsent older one,
23	 * so a stalled USB write can't accumulate stale state. Mode-level
24	 * arbitration (which producer is allowed to submit when) lives one
25	 * layer up; the link stays dumb. */
26

70	{
71	    if ((FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_CSR & (FLEX_US_CSR_OVRE_Msk | FLEX_US_CSR_FRAME_Msk | FLEX_US_CSR_PARE_Msk)) != 0U)

77	        while((FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_CSR & FLEX_US_CSR_RXRDY_Msk) != 0U)
78	        {
79	            if ((FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_MR & FLEX_US_MR_MODE9_Msk) != 0U)

93	{

95	    size_t rxSize = flexcom2UsartObj.rxSize;
96	
97	    if(flexcom2UsartObj.rxBusyStatus == true)
98	    {
99	        while(((FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_CSR & FLEX_US_CSR_RXRDY_Msk) != 0U) && (rxProcessedSize < rxSize))
100	        {
101	            if ((FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_MR & FLEX_US_MR_MODE9_Msk) != 0U)
102	            {
103	                ((uint16_t*)flexcom2UsartObj.rxBuffer)[rxProcessedSize] = (FLEXCOM_USART_RHR_9BIT_REG & (uint16_t)FLEX_US_RHR_RXCHR_Msk);
104	                rxProcessedSize++;
105	            }
106	            else
107	            {
108	                ((uint8_t*)flexcom2UsartObj.rxBuffer)[rxProcessedSize] = (FLEXCOM_USART_RHR_8BIT_REG);
109	                rxProcessedSize++;
110	            }
111	        }
112	
113	        flexcom2UsartObj.rxProcessedSize = rxProcessedSize;
114	
115	        /* Check if the buffer is done */
116	        if(rxProcessedSize >= rxSize)
117	        {
118	            flexcom2UsartObj.rxBusyStatus = false;
119	
120	            /* Disable Read, Overrun, Parity and Framing error interrupts */
121	            FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_IDR = (FLEX_US_IDR_RXRDY_Msk | FLEX_US_IDR_FRAME_Msk | FLEX_US_IDR_PARE_Msk | FLEX_US_IDR_OVRE_Msk);

149	                txProcessedSize++;
150	            }
151	            else
152	            {
153	                FLEXCOM_USART_THR_8BIT_REG =  ((uint8_t*)flexcom2UsartObj.txBuffer)[txProcessedSize];
154	                txProcessedSize++;
155	            }
156	        }
157

182	{

185	
186	    uint32_t interruptMask = FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_IMR;
187	
188	
189	    /* Error status */
190	    uint32_t errorStatus = (channelStatus & (FLEX_US_CSR_OVRE_Msk | FLEX_US_CSR_FRAME_Msk | FLEX_US_CSR_PARE_Msk));
191	
192	    if((errorStatus != 0U) && ((interruptMask & (FLEX_US_IMR_RXRDY_Msk | FLEX_US_IMR_FRAME_Msk | FLEX_US_IMR_PARE_Msk | FLEX_US_IMR_OVRE_Msk)) != 0U))
193	    {
194	        /* Save error to report it later */
195	        flexcom2UsartObj.errorStatus = errorStatus;
196	
197	        /* Clear error flags and flush the error data */
198	        FLEXCOM2_USART_ErrorClear();
199	
200	        /* Transfer complete. Clear the busy flag. */
201	        flexcom2UsartObj.rxBusyStatus = false;
202	
203	
204	        /* Disable Read, Overrun, Parity and Framing error interrupts */
205	        FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_IDR = (FLEX_US_IDR_RXRDY_Msk | FLEX_US_IDR_FRAME_Msk | FLEX_US_IDR_PARE_Msk | FLEX_US_IDR_OVRE_Msk);

207	        /* USART errors are normally associated with the receiver, hence calling receiver context */
208	        if( flexcom2UsartObj.rxCallback != NULL )
209	        {
210	            uintptr_t rxContext = flexcom2UsartObj.rxContext;
211	
212	            flexcom2UsartObj.rxCallback(rxContext);
213	        }
214	    }
215	
216	    /* Receiver status */
217	    if((channelStatus & FLEX_US_CSR_RXRDY_Msk) != 0U)
218	    {
219	        FLEXCOM2_USART_ISR_RX_Handler();
220	    }
221	
222	
223	    /* Transmitter status */
224	    if((channelStatus & FLEX_US_CSR_TXRDY_Msk) != 0U)
225	    {
226	        FLEXCOM2_USART_ISR_TX_Handler();
227	    }

232	void FLEXCOM2_USART_Initialize( void )
233	{
234	    /* Set FLEXCOM USART operating mode */
235	    FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_MR = FLEX_MR_OPMODE_USART;
236	
237	    /* Reset FLEXCOM2 USART */
238	    FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_CR = (FLEX_US_CR_RSTRX_Msk | FLEX_US_CR_RSTTX_Msk | FLEX_US_CR_RSTSTA_Msk );
239	
240	
241	    /* Setup transmitter timeguard register */
242	    FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_TTGR = 0;
243	
244	    /* Configure FLEXCOM2 USART mode */
245	    FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_MR = ( FLEX_US_MR_USART_MODE_NORMAL | FLEX_US_MR_USCLKS_MCK | FLEX_US_MR_CHRL_8_BIT | FLEX_US_MR_PAR_NO | FLEX_US_MR_NBSTOP_1_BIT | (0UL << FLEX_US_MR_OVER_Pos));
246	
247	    /* Configure FLEXCOM2 USART Baud Rate */
248	    FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_BRGR = FLEX_US_BRGR_CD(144) | FLEX_US_BRGR_FP(5);
249	
250	    /* Enable FLEXCOM2 USART */
251	    FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_CR = (FLEX_US_CR_TXEN_Msk | FLEX_US_CR_RXEN_Msk);
252	
253	
254	    /* Initialize instance object */
255	    flexcom2UsartObj.rxBuffer = NULL;
256	    flexcom2UsartObj.rxSize = 0;
257	    flexcom2UsartObj.rxProcessedSize = 0;
258	    flexcom2UsartObj.rxBusyStatus = false;
259	    flexcom2UsartObj.rxCallback = NULL;
260	    flexcom2UsartObj.errorStatus = FLEXCOM_USART_ERROR_NONE;
261	    flexcom2UsartObj.txBuffer = NULL;
262	    flexcom2UsartObj.txSize = 0;
263	    flexcom2UsartObj.txProcessedSize = 0;
264	    flexcom2UsartObj.txBusyStatus = false;
265	    flexcom2UsartObj.txCallback = NULL;
266	}

271

278	static void FLEXCOM2_USART_BaudCalculate(uint32_t srcClkFreq, uint32_t reqBaud, uint8_t overSamp, uint32_t* cd, uint32_t* fp, uint32_t* baudError)
279	{
280	    uint32_t actualBaud = 0U;
281	
282	    *cd = srcClkFreq / (reqBaud * 8U * (2U - overSamp));
283	
284	    if (*cd > 0U)
285	    {
286	        *fp = ((srcClkFreq / (reqBaud * (2U - (uint32_t)overSamp))) - ((*cd) * 8U));
287	        actualBaud = (srcClkFreq / (((*cd) * 8U) + (*fp))) / (2U - overSamp);
288	        *baudError = ((100U * actualBaud)/reqBaud) - 100U;
289	    }
290	}
291	
292	bool FLEXCOM2_USART_SerialSetup( FLEXCOM_USART_SERIAL_SETUP *setup, uint32_t srcClkFreq )
293	{
294	    uint32_t baud = 0;
295	    uint32_t overSampVal = 0;
296	    uint32_t usartMode;
297	    uint32_t cd0, fp0, cd1, fp1, baudError0, baudError1;
298	    bool status = false;
299	
300	    cd0 = fp0 = cd1 = fp1 = baudError0 = baudError1 = 0U;
301	
302	    bool rxBusyStatus = flexcom2UsartObj.rxBusyStatus;
303	
304	    if((flexcom2UsartObj.txBusyStatus == true) || (rxBusyStatus == true))
305	    {
306	        /* Transaction is in progress, so return without updating settings */
307	        return false;
308	    }
309	
310	    if (setup != NULL)
311	    {
312	        baud = setup->baudRate;
313	
314	        if(srcClkFreq == 0U)
315	        {
316	            srcClkFreq = FLEXCOM2_USART_FrequencyGet();
317	        }
318	
319	        /* Calculate baud register values for 8x/16x oversampling values */
320	
321	        FLEXCOM2_USART_BaudCalculate(srcClkFreq, baud, 0, &cd0, &fp0, &baudError0);
322	        FLEXCOM2_USART_BaudCalculate(srcClkFreq, baud, 1, &cd1, &fp1, &baudError1);
323	
324	        if ( (!(cd0 > 0U && cd0 <= 65535U)) && (!(cd1 > 0U && cd1 <= 65535U)) )
325	        {
326	            /* Requested baud cannot be generated with current clock settings */
327	            return status;
328	        }
329	
330	        if ( ((cd0 > 0U) && (cd0 <= 65535U)) && ((cd1 > 0U) && (cd1 <= 65535U)) )
331	        {
332	            /* Requested baud can be generated with both 8x and 16x oversampling. Select the one with less % error. */
333	            if (baudError1 < baudError0)
334	            {
335	                cd0 = cd1;
336	                fp0 = fp1;
337	                overSampVal = (1UL << FLEX_US_MR_OVER_Pos) & FLEX_US_MR_OVER_Msk;
338	            }
339	        }
340	        else
341	        {
342	            /* Requested baud can be generated with either with 8x oversampling or with 16x oversampling. Select valid one. */
343	            if ((cd1 > 0U) && (cd1 <= 65535U))
344	            {
345	                cd0 = cd1;
346	                fp0 = fp1;
347	                overSampVal = (1UL << FLEX_US_MR_OVER_Pos) & FLEX_US_MR_OVER_Msk;
348	            }
349	        }
350	
351	        /* Configure FLEXCOM2 USART mode */
352	        usartMode = FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_MR;
353	        usartMode &= ~(FLEX_US_MR_CHRL_Msk | FLEX_US_MR_MODE9_Msk | FLEX_US_MR_PAR_Msk | FLEX_US_MR_NBSTOP_Msk | FLEX_US_MR_OVER_Msk);
354	        FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_MR = usartMode | ((uint32_t)setup->dataWidth | (uint32_t)setup->parity | (uint32_t)setup->stopBits | overSampVal);
355	
356	        /* Configure FLEXCOM2 USART Baud Rate */
357	        FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_BRGR = FLEX_US_BRGR_CD(cd0) | FLEX_US_BRGR_FP(fp0);
358	        status = true;
359	    }
360	
361	    return status;
362	}
363	
364	bool FLEXCOM2_USART_Read( void *buffer, const size_t size )
365	{
366	    bool status = false;
367	    if(buffer != NULL)
368	    {
369	        /* Check if receive request is in progress */
370	        if(flexcom2UsartObj.rxBusyStatus == false)
371	        {
372	            /* Clear errors that may have got generated when there was no active read request pending */
373	            FLEXCOM2_USART_ErrorClear();
374	
375	            /* Clear the errors related to pervious read requests */
376	            flexcom2UsartObj.errorStatus = FLEXCOM_USART_ERROR_NONE;
377	
378	            flexcom2UsartObj.rxBuffer = buffer;
379	            flexcom2UsartObj.rxSize = size;
380	            flexcom2UsartObj.rxProcessedSize = 0;
381	            flexcom2UsartObj.rxBusyStatus = true;
382	            status = true;
383	
384	
385	            /* Enable Read, Overrun, Parity and Framing error interrupts */
386	            FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_IER = (FLEX_US_IER_RXRDY_Msk | FLEX_US_IER_FRAME_Msk | FLEX_US_IER_PARE_Msk | FLEX_US_IER_OVRE_Msk);
387	
388	        }
389	    }
390	
391	    return status;
392	}
393	
394	bool FLEXCOM2_USART_Write( void *buffer, const size_t size )
395	{
396	    bool status = false;
397	    if(buffer != NULL)
398	    {
399	        /* Check if transmit request is in progress */
400	        if(flexcom2UsartObj.txBusyStatus == false)
401	        {
402	            flexcom2UsartObj.txBuffer = buffer;
403	            flexcom2UsartObj.txSize = size;
404	            flexcom2UsartObj.txProcessedSize = 0;
405	            flexcom2UsartObj.txBusyStatus = true;
406	            status = true;
407	
408	
409	            size_t txProcessedSize = flexcom2UsartObj.txProcessedSize;
410	            size_t txSize = flexcom2UsartObj.txSize;
411	
412	            /* Initiate the transfer by sending first byte */
413	            while(((FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_CSR & FLEX_US_CSR_TXRDY_Msk) != 0U) && (txProcessedSize < txSize))
414	            {
415	                if ((FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_MR & FLEX_US_MR_MODE9_Msk) != 0U)
416	                {
417	                    FLEXCOM_USART_THR_9BIT_REG = ((uint16_t*)flexcom2UsartObj.txBuffer)[txProcessedSize] & (uint16_t)FLEX_US_THR_TXCHR_Msk;
418	                }
419	                else
420	                {
421	                    FLEXCOM_USART_THR_8BIT_REG = ((uint8_t*)flexcom2UsartObj.txBuffer)[txProcessedSize];
422	                }
423	                txProcessedSize++;
424	            }
425	
426	            flexcom2UsartObj.txProcessedSize = txProcessedSize;
427	
428	            FLEXCOM2_REGS->FLEX_US_IER = FLEX_US_IER_TXRDY_Msk;
429	        }
430	    }
431	
432	    return status;
433	}

172	    TimingPipeline_Initialize();

174	    /* manual_control is a peer producer for direct UI-driven actuation
175	     * (game-menu navigation, manual test). UI buttons are authored in
176	     * Microchip Graphics Composer; the generated screenShow_Screen0
177	     * registers the event_Screen0_Button_Manual_* callbacks defined in
178	     * ui/manual_input.c, so no explicit bind step is needed here. */
179	    ManualControl_Initialize();
180	
181	    /* Drain task is launched last so every producer's queue handle is
182	     * already valid when the first records hit the sink. Marvin creates
183	     * all tasks pre-scheduler (Harmony brings the scheduler up after
184	     * APP_Initialize returns); xTaskCreateStatic before vTaskStartScheduler
185	     * is the standard FreeRTOS pattern. */

I've now got the full picture. Let me lay out the migration plan before touching anything.

## Context (what I found)

The new board is the **SAM9X75 Curiosity Hybrid**. The MCC port is already done by you:
- Commit `598d370` **removed USB Host** from the config and moved display/MIPI I²C to FLEXCOM8.
- Commit `3af09bc` **added FLEXCOM2** for the guitar link — pins `PA13 GUITAR_TX` / `PA14 GUITAR_RX`, plib generated and `FLEXCOM2_USART_Initialize()` already called in [initialization.c:335](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/initialization.c#L335).

So the firmware is mid-migration: FLEXCOM2 is initialized but unused, while [app.c:166](firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c#L166) still calls `USB_HOST_BusEnable` and [fretboard_link.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c) still drives the USB CDC host stack that no longer gets initialized. The link target is fretboard SERCOM1 (PB00 TX / PB01 RX) at **500000 baud, 8N1** — unchanged on the fretboard side (it was always a UART; only marvin's bridging changes).

The FLEXCOM2 plib is the **basic interrupt-driven (non-ring-buffer)** variant: `Write`/`Read` complete-on-exact-size, with callbacks. Key consequence for RX: between a Read completing and the next being armed, RXRDY is disabled, so reads must be re-armed in the ISR callback to avoid overruns on the continuous 240 Hz stream.

## Plan

**The public API stays identical** (`FretboardLink_Initialize` / `_Send` / `_IsConnected`), so `timing_pipeline`, `manual_control`, and the host `marvin-perf` tooling are untouched.

**1. Rewrite [fretboard_link.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c)** — swap transport USB CDC host → FLEXCOM2 USART:
- *Remove:* all `usb/*` includes, CDC handle/attach/detach machinery, `open_cdc`/`close_cdc`, line-coding + DTR control-line-state, `s_ctrl_done`, `cdc_attach_handler`, `cdc_event_handler`.
- *TX:* register a write-complete callback (gives `s_write_done`, emits the `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` perf stamp from ISR); `send_one_byte` → `FLEXCOM2_USART_Write(&tx_byte,1)` + wait on semaphore with timeout. Same shape as today.
- *RX:* keep `s_rx_stream` + `fretboard_rx_task` + the 17-byte resync parser **verbatim**. Change the per-read chunk to `DS_FRAME_LEN` (17) so reads align with the fretboard's 17-byte bursts and the re-arm gap lands in the ~3.8 ms inter-frame idle (no overrun). `arm_rx_read` → `FLEXCOM2_USART_Read`; read-complete callback pushes `ReadCountGet()` bytes into the stream buffer, consumes any `ErrorGet()` status, re-arms.
- *Connection model:* no enumeration — a UART is always "up." Replace `s_connected` with a simple `s_link_up` set true after `Initialize`.
- *Initialize:* `FLEXCOM2_USART_SerialSetup(500000, 8N1)`, register both callbacks, arm first RX read; drop the CDC attach-handler registration. Both tasks (`FretLink`, `FretRx`) and perf-log task registration stay.

**2. [fretboard_link.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.h)** — update the doc comment (USB CDC host → FLEXCOM2 UART).

**3. [app.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c)** — remove `app_usb_host_event_handler`, the `VBUS_AH_PC27/PC31` enables, `USB_HOST_EventHandlerSet`, and `USB_HOST_BusEnable` + log line; update the surrounding comments.

**4. Docs** (per CLAUDE.md): marvin [spec.md](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md) §2.1 diagram, §3.1/§3.2 tables, §4.3, §1.4 status; top-level [SPEC.md](SPEC.md) diagram + M2 line; marvin [journal.md](firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md) decision-log + session entry (incl. noting USB-host re-apply patches #5/#7 are now moot on the hybrid board, and that the `CDC_*` perf-stage names are now historical but kept to avoid host schema churn).

**Notes / deliberate choices:**
- Keeping the perf-log stage enum names (`PERF_STAGE_CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE`, `PERF_STAGE_FBL_READ_COMPLETE`) so the host decoder needs no change — they're just stage IDs now.
- **Fallback if RX overruns on hardware:** regenerate FLEXCOM2 in MCC "Ring Buffer" mode (continuous ISR-fed ring, no re-arm gap) + a small RX-drain rewrite. Recommend starting with the basic plib since it reuses the existing architecture and needs no regen.
- Not touching USB *device*/UDPHS (perf-log path) or the fretboard firmware.

In the MCC FLEXCOM2 (USART) component:

| Setting | Value |

| **Operating mode** | Ring Buffer Mode (enable; this is the "USART Ring Buffer Mode" / interrupt-driven ring option — applies to both TX and RX) |

```c
#include "fretboard_link.h"

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"
#include "queue.h"
#include "semphr.h"

#include "definitions.h"
#include "log.h"
#include "timing_pipeline.h"
#include "perf_log/perf_log.h"
#include "video/video.h"
#include "game/fret.h"

#define FBL_TASK_STACK_WORDS    768u
#define FBL_TASK_PRIORITY       5u

#define FBL_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH     1u   /* latest-wins via xQueueOverwrite */

#define FBL_RX_TASK_STACK_WORDS 512u

#define DS_FRAME_LEN            17u
#define DS_START_BYTE           0x03u
#define DS_END_BYTE             0xFCu

/* RX notification threshold: wake the parse task once a full frame's worth of
 * bytes has landed in the FLEXCOM2 RX ring. The ring (sized in MCC) keeps
 * receiving continuously, so there is no per-read re-arm gap to lose bytes
 * across. */
#define FBL_RX_THRESHOLD        DS_FRAME_LEN

/* Idle heartbeat: re-send last mask if the timing pipeline goes quiet, so
 * a stalled detector or paused game can't leave a stale frets-active
 * pattern stuck on the wire. 50 ms is well below human-perceptible. */
#define FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS        50u

/* Bound the RX wait so a missed notification can't wedge the parser; the
 * stream is continuous at 240 Hz so a wake normally arrives every ~4 ms. */
#define FBL_RX_WAIT_MS          100u

/* Link runs at 500 000 baud, 8N1 — configured by the MCC FLEXCOM2 USART
 * component (FLEXCOM2_USART_Initialize). Must match the fretboard SERCOM1
 * setting or every byte arrives corrupt. */

static QueueHandle_t s_cmd_queue;
static StaticQueue_t s_cmd_queue_buf;
static uint8_t       s_cmd_queue_storage[FBL_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(uint8_t)];

static StackType_t   s_task_stack[FBL_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t  s_task_tcb;

static StackType_t   s_rx_task_stack[FBL_RX_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t  s_rx_task_tcb;

/* Given from the FLEXCOM2 read callback (ISR) when the RX ring crosses the
 * frame threshold; woken thread drains and parses. */
static SemaphoreHandle_t s_rx_notify;
static StaticSemaphore_t s_rx_notify_buf;

/* A UART has no enumeration step — the link is up once Initialize has armed
 * the peripheral. Kept so producers and the heartbeat path can gate sends. */
static volatile bool s_link_up;

/* Asserted-mask snapshot: most recent byte accepted into the FLEXCOM2 TX ring.
 * Producer-side intent goes out on the same wire byte but may be overwritten
 * before it transmits if Send is called faster than the link services. The
 * PERF_REC_ACTUATOR record carries both. */
static volatile uint8_t  s_last_sent_byte;

/* Last send result + timestamp, snapshotted into the ACTUATOR record so the
 * host can read Send-to-ack latency. A ring-buffer Write copies the byte and
 * returns immediately, so "ack" is the enqueue instant. */
static volatile int32_t  s_last_ack_result;
static volatile uint64_t s_last_ack_ts_counter;

static void rx_event_handler(FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT event, uintptr_t context)
{
    (void)context;
    BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;

    switch (event)
    {
        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_THRESHOLD_REACHED:
        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_BUFFER_FULL:
            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);
            break;
        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_ERROR:
            /* Consume + clear the error status; the resync parser recovers
             * frame alignment on the next valid start/end pair. */
            (void)FLEXCOM2_USART_ErrorGet();
            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);
            break;
        default:
            break;
    }

    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
}

static bool send_one_byte(uint8_t mask)
{
    if (!s_link_up) { return false; }

    uint8_t tx_byte = (uint8_t)(mask & 0x7F);

    /* Ring-buffer Write copies the byte into the TX ring and returns the
     * count accepted; for a single byte this only fails if the TX ring is
     * full, which shouldn't happen at command rates. */
    if (FLEXCOM2_USART_Write(&tx_byte, 1u) != 1u)
    {
        LOG_WARN("FBL: TX ring full, byte dropped\r\n");
        return false;
    }
    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_FBL_SEND, 0u, (uint32_t)tx_byte);

    s_last_sent_byte      = tx_byte;
    s_last_ack_result     = 0;
    s_last_ack_ts_counter = SYS_TIME_Counter64Get();
    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE, 0u, 0u);
    return true;
}

static void fretboard_link_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    LOG_INFO("FBL: fretboard link started (FLEXCOM2)\r\n");

    uint8_t last_mask = 0u;

    for (;;)
    {
        uint8_t mask;
        if (xQueueReceive(s_cmd_queue, &mask, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
        {
            last_mask = mask;
        }
        else
        {
            mask = last_mask;
        }

        (void)send_one_byte(mask);
    }
}

/* Drain the FLEXCOM2 RX ring and emit one PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW per parsed
 * 17-byte frame. Resync logic mirrors tools/ds_monitor.py: a frame is valid
 * only when buf[0]==0x03 AND buf[16]==0xFC; otherwise drop the leading byte
 * and retry alignment. The FSM-free buffered approach is easier to reason
 * about than a state machine and the frame is short. */
static void fretboard_rx_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    uint8_t  frame[DS_FRAME_LEN];
    size_t   filled = 0u;
    uint32_t parsed = 0u;
    uint32_t skipped_bytes = 0u;

    for (;;)
    {
        if (FLEXCOM2_USART_ReadCountGet() == 0u)
        {
            (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_rx_notify, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_RX_WAIT_MS));
            continue;
        }

        size_t want = DS_FRAME_LEN - filled;
        size_t got  = FLEXCOM2_USART_Read(&frame[filled], want);
        if (got == 0u) { continue; }
        filled += got;
        if (filled < DS_FRAME_LEN) { continue; }

        if (frame[0] != DS_START_BYTE || frame[DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u] != DS_END_BYTE)
        {
            /* Misaligned: drop one byte and shift, then loop to refill. */
            memmove(&frame[0], &frame[1], DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u);
            filled = DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u;
            skipped_bytes++;
            continue;
        }

        uint16_t adc[FRET_COUNT];
        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
        {
            adc[i] = (uint16_t)frame[1u + i * 2u]
                   | (uint16_t)((uint16_t)frame[2u + i * 2u] << 8);
        }

        /* seq: u32 LE at bytes 11-14, applied_mask: u8 at byte 15. */
        uint32_t fb_seq = (uint32_t)frame[11]
                        | ((uint32_t)frame[12] << 8)
                        | ((uint32_t)frame[13] << 16)
                        | ((uint32_t)frame[14] << 24);
        uint8_t  applied_mask = frame[15];

        Video_FrameInfo info;
        Video_GetFrameInfo(&info);
        PerfLog_EmitFretboardRaw(adc, info.frame_count, fb_seq, applied_mask);
        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_FBL_READ_COMPLETE, 0u, fb_seq);

        parsed++;
        if (parsed == 1u || (parsed % 240u) == 0u)
        {
            LOG_DEBUG("FBL: rx parsed=%u skipped=%u G=%u R=%u Y=%u B=%u O=%u\r\n",
                      (unsigned)parsed, (unsigned)skipped_bytes,
                      (unsigned)adc[0], (unsigned)adc[1], (unsigned)adc[2],
                      (unsigned)adc[3], (unsigned)adc[4]);
        }

        filled = 0u;
    }
}

void FretboardLink_Initialize(void)
{
    s_cmd_queue = xQueueCreateStatic(FBL_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH,
                                     sizeof(uint8_t),
                                     s_cmd_queue_storage,
                                     &s_cmd_queue_buf);
    configASSERT(s_cmd_queue != NULL);

    s_rx_notify = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_rx_notify_buf);
    configASSERT(s_rx_notify != NULL);

    /* Arm continuous RX: the ring fills from the FLEXCOM2 ISR; persistent
     * threshold notification wakes fretboard_rx_task each time a frame's
     * worth of bytes is available. */
    FLEXCOM2_USART_ReadCallbackRegister(rx_event_handler, 0u);
    FLEXCOM2_USART_ReadThresholdSet(FBL_RX_THRESHOLD);
    (void)FLEXCOM2_USART_ReadNotificationEnable(true, true);

    s_link_up = true;

    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_link_task,
                                       "FretLink",
                                       FBL_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
                                       NULL,
                                       FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
                                       s_task_stack,
                                       &s_task_tcb);
    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK, h);

    TaskHandle_t hr = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_rx_task,
                                        "FretRx",
                                        FBL_RX_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
                                        NULL,
                                        FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
                                        s_rx_task_stack,
                                        &s_rx_task_tcb);
    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_RX, hr);
}

bool FretboardLink_IsConnected(void)
{
    return s_link_up;
}

void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask, uint8_t producer_id)
{
    if (s_cmd_queue == NULL) { return; }
    uint8_t v = (uint8_t)(mask & TIMING_BIT_VALID_MASK);
    /* Overwrite is strictly latest-wins: a newer producer's mask replaces
     * any unsent older one — keeps a stalled write from accumulating
     * stale chord state. */
    (void)xQueueOverwrite(s_cmd_queue, &v);

    uint8_t strum_dir = 0u;
    if      (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN) { strum_dir = 1u; }
    else if (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP)   { strum_dir = 2u; }

    PerfLog_EmitActuator(v, s_last_sent_byte, strum_dir, producer_id,
                         s_last_ack_result, s_last_ack_ts_counter);
}

Next: pick the v0 algorithm (Q8) and start populating `fret[]`.

24	## Decision log
25	
26	| Date | Decision | Rationale |
27	|------|----------|-----------|
28	| 2026-06-03 | **Timing pipeline commands "released-style" play.** The release-suppression in `process_releases` ([timing_pipeline.c](../default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c)) was unbounded — it held a fret if *any* queued note/strum needed it, however far out, so across consecutive same-fret notes the fret stayed asserted the whole time. Bounded it: suppress the release only if the fret is re-needed at/before its own scheduled release time (`s_release_at_ms`), i.e. genuinely back-to-back; otherwise release for a clean per-note command. Helpers `note_q_any_needs`/`strum_q_any_needs` → `*_needs_by(bit, by_ms)`. Sustains are unaffected (continuous detector `pressed` → no release edge → never enters this path). | The legato hold was injecting marvin's note-queue lookahead into the emitted command, which polluted the edge-ai fret labels (the held fret reads `1` over a gap where the photosensor is bright). Proven by the detector-fb probe: clean per-note labels took overfit frets 0.94→0.99 (edge-ai journal 2026-06-03). Releasing per-note makes the command a function of the observable. Physical legato (avoiding release/repress churn on fast Expert runs) moves to a future fretboard *lazy actuator* layer; until then marvin's own play release-represses, which is fine at hard-mode note spacing. Validate marvin still plays hard cleanly after the change. |
29	| 2026-06-03 | **Perf-log schema v3→v4** (`PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped). `perf_rec_fretboard_raw_t` grows: its `reserved u16` becomes `fb_sample_seq (u32) + applied_mask (u8) + reserved (u8)` (28→32 B). `PerfLog_EmitFretboardRaw` gains `fb_sample_seq, applied_mask` params; `fretboard_link.c` RX parser reads the now-17-byte fretboard frame and passes them through. Host `marvin-perf` bumped to `EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION=4` in lockstep. | Unlike the 2026-06-02 *additive* FretboardRaw add (no bump), this changes an existing record's layout, so it must bump the version — the host's `check_schema` rejects mismatched streams. The two new fields are stamped by the fretboard itself (fretboard journal 2026-06-03) so the edge-ai training label (actuator state) is paired atomically with the ADC scan at the source; marvin's previous cross-TX/RX-clock reconstruction skewed the pairing and floored strum timing at ~20 ms in Phase-2 (edge-ai journal). Old `.bin` captures no longer decode under the new host — acceptable for dev; we re-capture. Wire-format break: fretboard + marvin must flash together. |
30	| 2026-06-02 | New `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` record type (`0x0B`) + `PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_RX` task slot (17). Default-disabled at boot like the other high-rate types; host enables via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`. `fretboard_link` gains a continuously-rearming `USB_HOST_CDC_Read` plus a sibling `fretboard_rx_task` that pops bytes off a 512 B stream buffer and emits one record per valid 12-byte fretboard data frame at the fretboard's 240 Hz rate. No `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump — additive only. | Step 1 of the Edge-AI training-dataset workstream: `cv_marvin_v1` provides the reference label per video frame, fretboard ADC samples are the input the future Edge-AI MCU would see. Routing both signals through the perf log lets one offline tool join them on `frame_epoch` (~4 fretboard records per video frame) and `ts_counter` (sub-frame ordering), which is the cheapest path to a labelled dataset before the SD recorder (§4.6) exists. Sibling task instead of folding RX into `fretboard_link_task` keeps the existing TX path untouched (its `xQueueReceive` blocking shape doesn't compose with a stream buffer without bigger surgery). The downstream `adc_fretboard` detector (§4.2, M2) is the natural follow-up; the bus scaffold (`DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD = 1`) is already reserved. |

Migration complete. Here's the summary.

## What changed

**Transport: USB CDC host → direct FLEXCOM2 USART** (PA13 TX / PA14 RX ↔ fretboard SERCOM1 PB01 RX / PB00 TX, 500000 Bd 8N1, ring-buffer mode). The fretboard end is unchanged — it was always a SERCOM1 UART; only marvin's side was USB-bridged.

- **[fretboard_link.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c)** — gutted the USB stack (CDC handle/attach/detach, `open_cdc`/`close_cdc`, line-coding + DTR, the `s_rx_stream` buffer and ISR re-arm). 285 lines deleted, 131 added.
  - *TX:* `FLEXCOM2_USART_Write(&byte, 1)` — synchronous enqueue, no ack semaphore.
  - *RX:* persistent read-threshold notification → ISR gives `s_rx_notify` → `fretboard_rx_task` drains the ring and runs the **unchanged** `0x03 … 0xFC` resync + `PerfLog_EmitFretboardRaw`. The ring *is* the buffer now.
  - `s_connected` → `s_link_up` (a wire is always up).
  - **Public API and every perf-log record/stamp preserved** → `timing_pipeline`, `manual_control`, and host `marvin-perf` need zero changes.
- **[app.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c)** — removed the USB-host include, event handler, VBUS enables, and `USB_HOST_BusEnable`.
- **[fretboard_link.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.h)** — header comment rewritten.
- **Docs** — marvin [spec.md](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md) (§1.3, §1.4, §2.1 diagram, §3.1, §3.2, §4.3), top-level [SPEC.md](SPEC.md) (diagram + M2), marvin [journal.md](firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md) (decision + session entries, obsolete patches #5/#7 annotated, current-focus lead).

firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:836:Root cause: the USB MCC regen reordered SYS_Initialize so `MMU_Initialize` and `AIC_INT_Initialize` ran *after* `TC0_CH0_TimerInitialize`, `FLEXCOM6_TWI_Initialize`, and `XLCDC_Initialize`. With AIC initialized late, the FLEXCOM6 interrupt vector wasn't owned by the AIC when the first I²C transfer ran; `OSAL_SEM_Pend(transferDone, WAIT_FOREVER)` blocked forever waiting for an ISR that never fired. FBL stayed alive because it's pure FreeRTOS — no peripheral interrupt dependency.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:838:Fix: reverted SYS_Initialize order so MMU/AIC/WDT-disable run before TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC. Display + capture came back on first boot. Logged as patch #6 in the MCC re-apply list above.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal-archive.md:22:  - I2C: FLEXCOM6 @ 400 kHz (see `default/src/config/default/configuration.h:102`)
firmware/marvin/docs/journal-archive.md:54:Nothing blocking Phase 1. I2C path is unambiguous: FLEXCOM6 on PA24/PA25 → J29 pins 21/20 → 22→15 adapter → Waveshare CAM_I²C → TC358743 at `0x0f`.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal-archive.md:60:**Result:** DBGU reports `TC358743: present (chipid=0x0000)` on every boot — TC358743 is on the bus at `0x0f`, ACKs our transactions, accepts the software reset, and returns a clean CHIPID read. Full I2C path validated end-to-end: FLEXCOM6 → PA24/PA25 → J29 → 22→15 adapter → Waveshare → TC358743.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal-archive.md:74:- The FLEXCOM6 I2C driver is already brought up by `SYS_Initialize` (`initialization.c:360`, `sysObj.drvI2C0 = DRV_I2C_Initialize(...)`), so the TC358743 module only needs `DRV_I2C_Open(DRV_I2C_INDEX_0, DRV_IO_INTENT_EXCLUSIVE)`.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal-archive.md:128:- I2C NAK on the first SYSCTL write → wrong slave address (`0x0f` wrong — check A0 pin tie-off on Waveshare), or the cable/adapter is backwards, or PA24/PA25 aren't muxed to FLEXCOM6.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal-archive.md:146:TC358743 has 16-bit register addresses and mixed 8/16/32-bit data widths. Port the Linux driver's `i2c_wr*` + `i2c_rd*` family, one-for-one, against FLEXCOM6 TWI.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal-archive.md:1479:`chipid=0x0000` satisfies the kernel driver's probe rule (high byte must be zero). I2C path from SAM9X75 FLEXCOM6 → J29 pins 20/21 → 22→15 adapter → Waveshare → TC358743 is fully validated. Software reset over I2C confirmed working. Non-blocking state machine and `SYS_TIME` delays behave as designed.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal-archive.md:1527:- Corrected J29 22-pin pinout via Microchip MCP query (User Guide §3.4.10): PC19 is on **pin 17** (`MIPI_CSI_GPIO0`), PC15 is on **pin 18** (`MIPI_CSI_GPIO1`). Pins 5/6 are CSI data lane 1 diff pairs, not GPIOs. I2C (PA24/PA25) on pins 21/20 confirmed against marvin's FLEXCOM6 pin assignments.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal-archive.md:1541:- Phase 2 register helpers will be a near-verbatim port of the kernel driver's `i2c_rd/wr*` family, mapped to FLEXCOM6 TWI.

marvin: move fretboard link from USB CDC host to FLEXCOM2 USART

The SAM9X75 Curiosity Hybrid board has no host-capable USB port, so the
EDBG-CDC-bridge transport for the fretboard link is gone. Talk UART
directly to the fretboard SERCOM1 instead: PA13 FLEXCOM2_IO0 (TX) /
PA14 FLEXCOM2_IO1 (RX) <-> fretboard PB01 RX / PB00 TX, 500000 Bd 8N1.

fretboard_link.c rewrite:
- FLEXCOM2 USART in ring-buffer mode (RX ring fills from its own ISR,
  no re-arm gap to overrun the continuous 240 Hz stream).
- RX: persistent read-threshold notification wakes fretboard_rx_task,
  which drains the ring and runs the unchanged 0x03..0xFC resync. The
  separate stream buffer + ISR re-arm are deleted (the ring is the buffer).
- TX: synchronous FLEXCOM2_USART_Write; drop the USB Write/ack semaphore.
- s_connected -> s_link_up (a UART is always up; no enumeration).
- Public API and all perf-log records/stamps preserved, so timing_pipeline,
  manual_control, and host marvin-perf are untouched.

app.c: remove the USB host include, event handler, VBUS enables, and
USB_HOST_BusEnable.

Docs: spec.md (S1.3/1.4/2.1/3.1/3.2/4.3), top-level SPEC.md, and the marvin
journal updated for the FLEXCOM2 link. Also reconciled the FLEXCOM6 ->
FLEXCOM8 TWI doc drift (TC358743 control I2C moved to PB4/PB5 during the
Hybrid port); dated journal/archive entries kept as historical record.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
